Its remaining source-derived boundary was that transitions which keep the member in a configuration half leave the gate armed, and this is exactly what a positive control can settle: a joint-explicit removal that is never left keeps the member as an outgoing voter, so if the gate stays armed its proposals must be accepted and committed while every other condition of the witness scenario is unchanged apart from the missing removal from both halves.

investigations.hypothesis: The node.run() removal guard is guarded by the disappearance of the local Progress entry, which LeaveJoint performs for outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set, while EnterJoint keeps the entry for outgoing voters. investigations.question: After a voter is removed and then re-added by committed configuration changes, which code path lets a Node.Propose invocation on that re-added voter reach a decision (forward to the leader, be appended, or return an error), while the same leader stays in place?

result.summary: Submitting a decisive positive control for the primary finding's necessary premise, attached to a child investigation of the explained parent. The parent account rests on the removal guard firing because the local progress entry disappears, and its remaining source-derived boundary was that a member kept in a configuration half should keep its gate armed; this experiment settles that boundary by construction. It runs the same three-node Node-API cluster, elects leader 1, proposes a joint-explicit removal of node 3 that is never left, waits until node 3's own configuration lists it in the outgoing half while still counting it as a voter, and then invokes Propose on node 3 with two comparisons: the invocation returned, and its payload was committed. The cited anchor is the LeaveJoint deletion of outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set, which is exactly the transition the guard reacts to. Local verification of the new test shows the predicted difference: node 3 is an outgoing voter per its own status, its invocation returned in 0 ms with no error, and the payload was committed on all three nodes, while the witness scenario with the member dropped from both halves left the same invocation pending for its whole window. Both comparisons were dry-run through the framework's own comparator against the local event stream and evaluate as complete holds, so the successor receipt should be cleanly interpretable and will let the parent interpretation state the premise as witnessed rather than source-derived.

investigations.question: After a voter is removed and then re-added by committed configuration changes, which code path lets a Node.Propose invocation on that re-added voter reach a decision (forward to the leader, be appended, or return an error), while the same leader stays in place?
investigations.hypothesis: node.run() keeps its proposal gate armed only as a side effect of observing a leader change and disarms it when the local member is removed from the configuration; a re-admission does not re-arm it, so while no leader change is observed the member's MsgProp traffic (Node.Propose and Node.ProposeConfChange) stays pending on the non-nil n.propc channel instead of being forwarded, appended, or rejected with an error. Retained evidence (six-signal lineage): with the leader unchanged the invocation does not return inside the observed windows, payloads are not committed, an invocation with a context that never expires stays pending, the same call succeeds and commits once leadership changes, and a never-removed member's proposals commit throughout.

scope.description: Exploration with no fixed requirement: three real raft state machines (ids 1,2,3, ElectionTick 10, HeartbeatTick 1, in-memory storage whose ConfState is {1,2,3}) driven for 300 steps per seed, with random connectivity masks that change the reachable peers, per-message drop decisions, random ticks, random proposals from members, random campaigns and random leader transfer requests. Committed entries are applied through the captured log interface, and safety monitors run after every step: one leader per term, applied entries immutable per node and index, identical entry for the same index across nodes, committed index monotonic per node, and every previously applied entry present in the log of a state machine that reports itself leader. Events report any violation with seed, invariant and detail, and one summary per seed with the exercised counts.
assumptions: Messages are delivered in random batches of up to three per step and may be dropped, which models lossy, reordering-prone transport without permanent partitions.
The confinement masks change independently per node, so asymmetric partitions occur.
Entries are persisted to the in-memory storage through the captured helpers before messages are delivered, matching the documented usage.
No configuration changes are injected in this exploration; membership transitions are covered by the deterministic experiments.
excluded: Membership changes, snapshot transfer and restart recovery (covered by deterministic experiments or left for later)
Crash-stop faults: state machines keep running for the whole scenario
Any claim of absence of defects beyond the two explored seeds and 300 steps each
